explain: Hazardous conditions like an unguarded railway crossing are categorized as Warning (Cautionary) signs, typically triangular in shape.

q: 2. The usual width of side drains along Highways in hilly region, is
explain: Standard hill road drains are typically 60 cm wide (often trapezoidal or V-shaped).

q: 3. In retaining and breast walls, weep holes are provided at
options: 50 cm vertical height and 50 cm c/c horizontally
100 cm vertical height and 100 cm c/c horizontally
100 cm vertical height and 120 cm c/c horizontally
120 cm vertical height and 100 cm c/c horizontally
explain: Weep holes are placed at roughly 1-meter intervals (100 cm) both ways to drain water and prevent hydrostatic pressure build-up.

q: 4. Along a hill road, a side drain is provided on
options: outer side of a spur curve
outer side of a re-entrant curve
explain: Water is always directed toward the hill-side (inner side) to prevent it from washing over the embankment edge and causing erosion.

q: 5. Intermediate catch water drains are provided only, if
options: catchment area of the watershed above road is large
single catch water drain is inadequate
explain: Catch water drains prevent surface runoff from the hill above from reaching the road; multiple drains are needed if the volume is too high for one.

q: 6. The side drains are provided on both sides of the roadway, when the road is ............
explain: When a road is in a deep cutting, water from both side slopes must be collected, requiring drains on both sides of the road.
A 'Level Crossing' sign alerts the driver to a potential hazard ahead (the railway crossing), making it a cautionary or warning sign.
